notes.note: 19 tackles and 29 disposals with a fantastic game for Berry.
Cook really bounced back this week with 19 disposals at 94% efficiency. We may see some inconsistent scoring from him but try and loop him on where you can.
This was now two really low scores from Cook in a row with just the 11 disposals this week. If you have the trades then move him on.
Cook had just the 8 disposals at 50% efficiency and his lowest score by some distance this season. You should only have him on your bench going forward. If not you need to upgrade him.
This was the best we have seen from Cook in the last five games as he posted 21 disposals in the win.
19 and a goal for Cook in the win as he continues to hang around that 65-75 scoring range for the fourth game in a row. He should be in your upgrade plans.
Cook missed that BE with another score under 75 making it now three in a row. He isn't our most critical trade out but he is one that you could consider upgrading
Cook missed his BE and had his lowest in the last month. Not to be concerned here as he didn't drop much value and is on his bye this week so time to trade him anyway. He has done his job.

Cook is continuing to provide us with some great value and good scoring. 15 disposals and a goal and he is a good user of the footy which helps his score. His BE is in the 70s now which means his money growth is at its limit
Solid from Cook with 22 disposals and 7 marks. He is still beating that BE and he is a safe to play on field. The hope is we can get him through to the byes.
The winning goal from Cook certainly helped boost his score but he had a good game as well with 21 disposals.  Nothing to worry about here he is still making money and is fieldable.
Cook continues to post some great scores and is very fieldable for you. 20 disposals and importantly he has good job security. His BE is still low so keep playing him.
This was the best for the year for Cook which will see his value rise nicely for a couple of weeks. 19 touches and a goal at a very handy 89% efficiency. He has been a great pick up.
Cook has had three in the 60s now and this looks to be his range now which whilst his BE is still low at 41 is fine to keep holding and he is safe for on field.
10 kicks and no handballs for Cook with a goal. This was his lowest score so far this season but far from concerning. He is scoring very well and still has a great BE.

Many coaches downgraded Petracca to Cook and that proved to be a great play with this score boosting his value and ensuring he will make more cash in coming weeks with a BE of -12. 21 disposals and 6 marks in the wet was a good result.
Cook couldn't back up last week's big outing as things were a little tighter against the Dogs. But he still posted a score that means he has a great BE that will see him a heavy trade in this week.
Cook was fantastic and deserved the hype he was given over recent weeks. 21 disposals to go with a goal. He will be a popular trade in
Curtin was the top scorer for the Crows starting on the wing this week. 26 disposals and 14 contested possessions.
Curtin injured a kneecap in the preseason so rule him out of your squads.
Dawson just keeps on performing for us with his 29 disposals and 2 goals this week. It is likely to be either Dawson or Rankine that will get the Jordon tag at the SCG this week.
Dawson was intercepting everything and had 27 disposals and 8 tackles He continues to be one of the best in the competition and a must have. Certainly consider him for a C or VC each week.
Dawson was the best for the Crows in the loss. He ended with 25 disposals and 6 tackles showing that even in a loss he can post a big score.
Dawson had Steele running with him and had two goals but just 18 disposals which is down by his standards. This was his first under 100 since round 5.
Dawson was outstanding as he set the win up from the very start. A 68 point first quarter set the foundation with his 3 goals 32 disposals and 7 clearances on the night. A must have.
Dawson was brought in by a lot of teams but some were wary of a tag but he had a big night kicking 3 goals and laying 9 tackles to go with 22 disposals. A great trade in if you need a mid.
Dawson was outstanding in the first term and finished with 9 tackles to go with 28 disposals and 12 contested possessions. He will be a hot target after the bye.
Dawson was the top scorer in the game with his 24 touches goal and 6 marks. He was back in the CBAs with 63% this week which is more than the last two games combined.
Dawson returned this week and put the Crows on his back at stages and ended with 12 marks 29 disposals and a goal. Look for him to hopefully continue with this form.
Dawson returned and was massive. He was taking kick ins as well as kicking 2 goals for his 28 disposals. He didn't spend as much time at CBAs at just 29%. His best score for the year.
Dawson posted his lowest so far this season and he couldn't get the space he wanted in the wet. Nothing to be concerned about here yet.
Dawson returned this week and slotted two goals to go with 23 disposals. He showed no signs of the injury that held him out last week.
Dawson missed this week but had it not been for the short turnaround could have played so hold him. He participated fully at training on Tuesday so it looks like he should be fine.
Dawson had a great second half and really dragged the Crows back into the game and this was reflected in his score. If not for his 64% efficiency he would have had a big score.
Dawson wasn't at his very best but did enough for us with his 21 touches. He did land very heavily on his back in the last minutes of the game but did get up.
Edwards dropped down from last week's score with just 12 disposals and only 6 were effective. With a BE of -24 he is still one you could downgrade to but that 39 does ring some alarms..
First game for Charlie did see 3 free kicks against but he also had 18 disposals and 5 clearances. If he can put up another game like this he is likely to be a popular trade in.

injury_suspension_status_text: Hamstring. Expected to be available for round 23.
Ankle. Expected recovery time is to be confirmed.

notes.note: Laird left the game in the second term with an ankle issue and didn't return. Reports are that he will miss 3-4 weeks.
Laird had been a popular trade in for Sinclair but he had his lowest in the last three games. The Crows have a good run home so he should be ok.
Laird was a popular replacement for Roberts and didn't disappoint with his 26 disposals and 10 marks. A handy pick up if you got him.
Laird injured a calf early in the game but did finish it out. He will miss 1 to 2 weeks.
McAndrew continues to impress with his 26 hit outs and 7 tackles.
McAndrew continues to post big scores. This was his second best for the season with 7 tackles a part of his good score. If you are running out of trades you can certainly hold him as R2.
McAndrew had a good battle with Sweet and his score certainly was helped with 8 tackles to go with his 14 disposals.
McAndrew had a tough day against Gawn and spent some time off after a collision with Lever.  Not his best but he is one you should be upgrading.
McAndrew continues to put up serviceable scores as he won the battle with English this week. He isn't a long term play as your R2 but he is doing enough for you at the moment.
McAndrew took full toll against the part time Geelong rucks. 51 hit outs and 16 disposals for his second best score of the season.
McAndrew got to 75 which did include a goal. He has done his job and now you should be looking to upgrade him to one of the top rucks.

McAndrew had a good day against Xerri and took the honour by virtue of his 2 goals but he sat on the pine for much of the last term when the game was well and truly over which did limit him to just 9 points in that term.
McAndrew dominated the hit outs against Balta with 33 to go with 9 disposals and a goal. He made his BE and with a new one of 53 he looks like we can hold til his bye.
McAndrew had a solid outing against Sweet with 11 disposals and 33 hit outs. With Richmond this week he should post a good score and beat his BE.

McAndrew had 30 hitouts and 11 disposals but at just 36% efficiency. He beat his BE but now has a BE of 73 so it could be time to upgrade him to one of the big two. He shouldn't drop sharply but he needs to be watched closely.

McAndrew got off to a slow start but finished well with 9 disposals and 29 hitouts against Marshall after TDK copped an early injury. His BE is still low at 51 but it won't be long before we need to either see another big game or trade out of him.
McAndrew didn't have it his own way against the stronger Pittonet. But he still did more than enough and remains a good R2 option.
McAndrew wasn't impacted at all by O'Brien being in the team and he made a statement with his best score of the season laying 13 tackles. He is looking like he could be a permanent R2 at this stage.
McAndrew continues to impress and importantly generate cash. Not his best score but also the conditions weren't friendly to big men. 40 hitouts and 17 disposals was a good return.
McAndrew had a great game against English with 38 hit outs and 13 disposals. As an R2 selection he is certainly paying off.
McAndrew was the R2 for many teams and he was great with 27 hitouts and 13 disposals. He did this against good opposition with Cameron before he faces English this week. This role is his for now.
McAndrew seems to have taken the number one ruck spot from O'Brien
27 touches and a rare goal for Milera but this is now three under 100 in a row for him.
Milera had that good role across half back and racked up 24 disposals and took 6 marks as he continues to do what we need from him.
20 kicks for Milera and 4 handballs. Not his huge score like last week but a good outing for owners despite just missing his BE.
Milera top scored in the game from his 32 disposals at 84% and 9 contested possessions. This is three over 120 in the last four games now.
Milera had just the 19 disposals but with the Crows in total control the ball wasn't in his area a great deal and the pressure wasn't there.
Milera was the second highest scorer in the game from his 32 disposals largely thanks to his efficiency of 94%. A great performance and his second over 120 in a row.
Milera had his third highest score of the season with 29 disposals at 93%. He has been a great hold for those that kept him after his two low scores.
Milera's lowest in the last four as the Lions had control of the game. He should be better this week against the Power.
Milera top scored for the Crows and has now put together 3 over 100 since many teams traded him out. 29 disposals at 93% and 9 marks.
Milera has now posted back to back over 100 with 25 disposals this week which included 5 kick ins which is the most he has had since round 1.
Milera showed some of the form we saw in round 1 with the best score for the Crows this week with 27 disposals at 92% efficiency.

Milera faded out of the game in the last term and didn't look to be at his best. Unfortunately his BE has risen to 137 as that first game washes out from his cycle so he is one you should try and trade out this week.
Milera had just 2 of the kick ins this week after taking 14 last week. Hopefully this is just a one off as the Crows back line was under real pressure.
Milera had his best game for a while as he racked up 34 disposals at 94% efficiency. Could this be his year!
O'Brien came into the side but played just 35% time on ground with 3 disposals and 15 hitouts. He had no impact on McAndrew's output.
O'Brien looks like he is set for extended stints in the SANFL with McAndrew looking like the preferred ruck option at Adelaide.
Rachele produced a great game for us this week thanks to his three goals and 17 disposals.

Rachele has been struggling to score of late and this is his best in the last three thanks to him having 17 disposals and a goal. He is one that you may want to loop as he can put in a low score more often than not.
Rachele kicked an early goal but really went missing after that having just 9 disposals. He did have 29% CBAs which was influenced when Rankine was off the ground with his ankle issue.
Rachele slotted 3 goals from his 17 disposals but an efficiency of just 52% really hurt that score. He would be a luxury trade if you have enough left or if you can loop him off the bench.

Rachele booted 4 goals on the way to his best score in the last 8 matches. The concern is that he needs goals to score as he had just 3% CBAs this week and when Rankine returns that will likely drop to 0.
Rachele attended 40% of the crows CBAs which was the most for him in 6 games but still finished with just 12 disposals and a sub 70 score. He is one that we need to look at moving on where we can.
Rachele didn't get the mid role after Rankine had to leave the game which is a real concern. His lowest score of the season and he is one that you could trade while he is on the bye this week.

Rachele had his second in the 80s in a row and was right on his BE but it did take 3 goals to get there. His CBAs were at just 9% which isn't ideal and he may be one we trade at the byes. This isn't the role we were promised for him.
Rachele spent a lot of time up forward attending just 15% of CBAs which isn't the role we want. But he did end with 2 goals from his 14 touches which boosted his score.
2 goals 3 for Rachele as this is now three in a row of 70 points or less for him. A huge concern for owners as he is losing value. The Crows have a good run to their bye so he should rebound.

Rachele has struggled now in the last two games with 15 disposals this week making it two poor scores in a row now. This is a real concern as we saw his CBAs drop down to 38% after 81% the week before.
Rachele couldn't back up last week's big scoring. Just 20 disposals and a goal for him. This is going to happen so don't panic on him.

Rachele has been on fire over the last three weeks ads he equalled the 127 he posted two weeks ago. He had just the 48% CBAs this week which is his second lowest of the season but the 4 goals were the key.
Rachele was again good and had 65% CBAs with his 19 disposals. If you need to get a forward he is one you can't go past. This is back to back weeks of CBAs in the mid 60s.
This was one of the best games we have seen Rachele play as he top scored for the Crows with a team high 7 clearances to go with 31 disposals. With Dawson out he attended 64% of the CBAs.
Rachele gave away 5 free kicks which really hurt his scoring. He had 18 disposals and 2 goals but the free kicks and 9 clangers make him someone that we may look at trading out.
Rachele managed 24 touches and a goal for a solid score as he had the role we want with 50% CBAs. The key will be what happens when Rankine returns next game.
This is the Rankine that we all expected to see this season and he was fantastic. 31 disposals 8 tackles and 7 clearances for him as he posted a huge score. Just beware of the Jordon tag this week.
Rankine racked up 27 disposals with this his best since his return but he is still dropping in value so you can afford to wait another week on him.

Rankine had a horror night with just 12 disposals at 50%. He did have some knee and ankle concerns after getting stuck under a tackle early but did finish the game out. He never really got going though.
Rankine returned to the team and was good in the first half but did slow after half time with just 14 of his points coming after half time. He will be better for the run and one to pick up soon.
Rankine looks like he could be back for round 15 and if so he will be a popular trade in.

Rankine was on fire early but left the game early in the third term with a calf injury. He is going to be missing for 3 weeks minimum but one of them is the bye. If not for the byes you could possibly hold but he isn't a guarantee to come back after that third week.

Had the tag early but once the game was done in the second he was released and ended with a game high in contested possessions and clearances with 15 and 10. This is the role we knew he would excel in. Best to wait til after R12 though.

Rankine was massive and dominated the game. 10 marks 9 tackles and 33 disposals to go with a goal. He does have a tricky run coming up with tags from Simpkin and Mullin a night game in Tasmania and a bye.
Rankine is certainly looking back to his best. He had 23 disposals and a goal and if not for that R12 bye he would be a great trade in.
This was more like Rankine. 11 contested possessions and 19 disposals with a couple of goals. This is now two good ones in the last three. He is starting to get back to the form we like to see.
1 goal 3 behinds for Rankine from his 20 disposals but it was the 40% efficiency that hurt his score. Just one score over 70 now in the last 4 isn't really what we were hoping for.

This is the Rankine that we were all expecting to see this season. 2 goals 7 tackles with 22 disposals. His BE is at 92 so you can hold off if you need to as his price shouldn't move upwards a significant amount this week without a huge score.
Rankine struggled again but was better than the previous week. 14 disposals and 3 behinds for him. His BE is still very high so we can watch him for another couple of weeks.
Rankine was tagged by Mullin and really didn't look at his best. He had 7 disposals 1 goal but gave away 3 free kicks. His price will plummet with a BE of 207 so don't go near him for a while.
Rankine returned to the team from his suspension and was quiet for the first half but did start to get into the game in the last where he kicked an important goal that boosted his score.
Rankine will miss round one through suspension
Thilthorpe was suspended for a week so will miss the next two rounds with the bye in there. It could do him some good as he still doesn't look like he is operating at 100%.
Worrell has had now 4 games over 100 for the season with another great game this week. 11 marks and 28 disposals at 92% as he is putting his hand up for a spot in our teams.
Andrews will be missing until Gather round after an errant swinging arm has seen him suspended for 3 games.

Annable didn't have a big outing in his first game despite 13 disposals. Just the 2 were contested and 240m gained. We can wait another week yet but another game like this will mean he is a correction trade.
We didn't see Annable in the Opening round clash so keep him as a downgrade target later

Will was massive this week with 8 clearances 3 goals and 33 disposals to go with 7 marks. He is one that wanted the ball in his hands and he ran with it scoring plenty of points even in time on in the last when the game was won.
Despite three behinds he top scored from the Lions with his 32 disposals. Four over 100 in the last five now for Ashcroft.

Back to back huge games for Ashcroft as he top scored for the Lions again this week. 30 disposals 8 clearances and 7 tackles. He is hitting a great run of form so he may be targeted by coaches needing a reliable midfielder.
Will went huge this week with his 2 goals coming from 38 disposals and 10 marks. Just his second over 100 since round 8 though despite how big it was.
22 touches for Ashcroft but his efficiency was just 59% as he posted another score under 90 making it four in the last five games.
Ashcroft was one of just 3 Lions to reach triple figures this week after a couple of goals from his 22 disposals.
Second lowest of the year for Ashcroft and he hasn't had a score over 100 now in the last four either. 21 disposals at 66% for him this week.
24 touches for Will but just 79% efficiency and his lowest since round 5
23 touches for Ashcroft and his lowest in the last month. We shouldn't be concerned as he is still scoring but he will need to be upgraded over the byes.
Will didn't have a huge day as the Lions spread the points around with 12 players on 90 or more. He ended with 28 disposals and 9 marks but his efficiency let him down.
26 disposals and a goal but 3 frees against meant that he had his second under 100 in a row.
Ashcroft had Simpkin for company for much of the game and was held to 19 disposals and his lowest for the season.
Will Ashcroft had his own footy and it looks to be his midfield now. 36 disposals and a goal for his best for the season by far.
2 goals for Bailey from 20 disposals in his third of 100+ in his last four games. He is certainly that forward option you could consider.
2 goals for Bailey from his 25 disposals and one of just 5 players in the game to reach triple figures.
Bailey had his best score for the last three games in the loss with his 17 disposals including 9 contested disposals.
Bailey has been a popular pick in recent weeks with some big scores but this week he had just the 14 disposals and didn't kick any goals. His second lowest score this year.
Berry was the top scorer in the game and best with 31 disposals and 10 marks. He has had one good and one poor score before this so he isn't a solid play just yet.
2 goals but just the 8 disposals. This was Charlie's lowest in the last four. His scoring can be quite up and down.
Coleman did a hamstring early in the game and had just 6 disposals. He is now going to miss a number of weeks and is a trade.
Coleman posted his lowest for the last four games and he just missed his BE. He is one that we could look to upgrade as he hasn't hit a ton since round 4.
Kiddy had the 18 disposals and a good efficiency at 88%. This makes it 6 weeks without triple figures for him.
Coleman put up 19 disposals and 7 marks but again missed his BE. You could be forgiven for upgrading him. He has 61 as a BE which is still achievable
Coleman was on the cusp of being traded out by a lot of sides but he stood up and took 11 marks and had 24 disposals.

Coleman had a poor day by the standards we have seen recently as Lincoln McCarthy took some of his points this week. This is now two poor ones in the last three and his BE at 78 means we may need to look at moving him on.
Coleman continues to deliver with his 20 disposals and 7 marks this week. He is showing us some solid form which we all knew he had in him.
Back to the scores from his early games for Coleman which is a concern for owners. His BE of 30 means we can wait still before we need to consider whether we trade him out.
Kiddy was great again this week with his 22 touches and 10 marks. His best for the season so far and he is looking fantastic. Well done for those that held.
This was what we were hoping for from Coleman with his 21 disposals coming at 85% efficiency. He is now at a BE of 7 so hold him.
Coleman was disappointing but the Lions weren't good. His BE of 22 means we could hold him and don't forget he is on bye this week.
Coleman did enough but his time on ground was low at just 74%. No reason to not select him though.
Draper hasn't been over 90 now in the last four games and isn't one that you want to be running in your ruck position.
Draper still has just the one big score this season even though this was better than last week. He had a solid game but really isn't up there with the best of the rucks this season.
Draper struggled again this week to score. He isn't an option.
Draper's first game for the Lions was a forgettable one with 3 behinds and just 8 hitouts and 8 disposals.
14 tackles certainly boosted Dunkley's score this week as he had just the 17 disposals. First back to back scores over 100 for him this season.
First over 100 for Dunkley since round 7.  The key was 9 tackles which was the most in the game.
Dunkley  led the Lions in Contested possessions and clearances for the week from his 22 disposals. This is back to back 80s now.
Dunkley wasn't his usual influential self with 15 of his 23 by hand. He isn't on our radar.
Dunkley's last two games have been better than opening round and he is still an option for us to keep an eye on.
Much better for Dunkley this week. 9 tackles to go with his 22 disposals. His price is going to drop and if we need to pick someone up after his bye we could consider him a fallen premium.
A quiet opening round for Dunkley. His price will fall so no need to rush him into your side.
Jaspa had one out of the box with his 10 marks and 27 disposals. Is this the break out game that will spark his run. Keep an eye on him.

injury_suspension_status_text: Hamstring. Expected to be available for round 24.

notes.note: McCluggage returned to the side and had 4 kicks with 12 handballs and a goal. He isn't one that we want to bring in
McCluggage missed this week after a calf issue at training. He is going to miss some games.
McCluggage struggled to score again this week having just 13 disposals and 2 marks. He is not performing as we had hoped and can be upgraded if you get the chance as he has a high BE.
McCluggage has been very frustrating for owners who got him in recently. He had a run of three games where he averaged 98 but has then averaged just 52 over the last two weeks.
McCluggage had a quiet game with just the 16 disposals and only half were contested. This was his second in the 60s since his return. Importantly his TOG went up again.

McCluggage led the game in clearances with 11 and had the third most contested possessions with 13. This was his first over 100 and he did all this in 77% TOG which is the most he has had this season.
McCluggage is building and was again good this week with 9 clearances and 12 contested possessions.
McCluggage's return hasn't heralded huge scores and he is still one that you don't need to consider unless he starts going on a tear.
McCluggage struggled in his second game back. His BE has stayed high at 185 so he is off the table for us for a while to come.
McCluggage returned to the side with 20 disposals. We need to see more from him before we look to bring him in. Particularly with a BE of 282.
Hugh left the opening round game in the first quarter with a calf injury. Watch the injury reports to see when he may return.
Unfortunately he dropped back to his mid 50s scoring this week despite 2 goals. This is going to happen with his game on occasion.
McKenna bobbed up for his best score this season with 2.3 to his name from his 18 disposals.
11 touches for McKenna as he made his BE but not by much. A trade needs to be considered soon.
7 goals for Morris as he had 17 kicks and no handballs with 9 marks.
Neale was big this week with 13 marks and 40 disposals. The Lions had it all their own way and Neale took full advantage of it.
Neale copped a head knock early and had to go off for a HIA which he passed. When he came back on he was released from the Mullin tag to end with 28 disposals.
Solid game for Neale without being a top end score. 27 touches and 7 clearances for him.  Just 122m gained due to 17 of those touches being handballs. Nothing to worry about here
Neale was quiet by his standards in the first half but a 37 point third term helped to change that as he was one of only three Lions over 100 this week.
This was Neale's best score of the season as he managed 37 disposals 10 clearances and 19 contested possessions. He was allowed to run as he pleased and hopefully can continue.
Neale struggled early but worked his way into the game. However he still posted his lowest score of the season.
Neale was one of just two Lions over 100 this week as he led the team in both contested possessions with 16 and 10 from his 32 disposals and 6 tackles.
Neale had the tag from Mullin but he still had 28 disposals to be the second best scorer for the Lions. Just his second under 100 in the last 7 games.

Neale topped the disposals for the game with 33 as he also took 8 marks and had 9 clearances. This makes it 5 over 110 in the last 6 for him as he is really looking a good unique pick with less than 10% of teams owning him.
Neale finished with a goal and 27 disposals but it was his first under 110 in the last five.
Huge day for Neale with 42 disposals and 13 marks after he left the game very early from a heavy bump to the chest.
Neale was one of the best for the lions in his 300th as he led the game in Contested possessions and clearances with 16 and 10. A good run of 3 games now.
Neale was the top scorer for the game with 30 disposals 20 contested disposals and 10 clearances to lead those two categories in the game.
First 100+ score since opening round for Lachie who looked a lot better this week than he has over recent games. He looked to be playing a with deal of freedom
This was a very quiet one from Neale with his 19 disposals being his lowest amount of touches for the season by 9.
Neale was still one of the best for the Lions despite the score. 28 disposals for him as he had the second most touches in the game.
Neale was the top possession getter in the game. Looked good to go for another great season.

injury_suspension_status_text: Knee. Out for season.

notes.note: Wilmot continues his good run with 9 marks and 26 disposals.
Wilmott put up his second over 100 in the last three weeks and he was the only Lion over 100. In recent weeks it has just been that 55 in round 9 that has been a bump in the road.
Wilmot was huge with 12 marks and 32 disposals. Easily his best of the year. But hold off until we see another game of this standard with his previous 5 only averaging 77.6
ZZ was a late inclusion for Fort which hurt a number of teams who used him as a Loop captain this week. He rose in value which is what we have been waiting for.
Solid from ZZ and just the score those that had him at R3 would have been looking for.
Zorko was back and he played well with his 32 touches and 4 marks. A good return for the Lions star.
Zorko was a late out 'managed' so just watch to see if it was something more serious.
19 disposals for Zorko and just the 4 marks. This is well down for him and it was his worst score this year apart from the game he was injured in.
Zorko returned and it was like he hadn't left with 13 marks to go with 27 disposals and the third most points for the Lions. His BE tells us we can wait another week with a BE of 148.
Keep an eye on teams there is talk he could be back soon.
We saw Zorko leave the game in the second term with a calf injury that looks like he is going to miss a few weeks. He is  going to need to be a trade.

Zorko took 9 marks with his 28 disposals. He didn't get to his BE however his price won't fluctuate too much as his scoring is quite consistent in this range. He is going to be someone to have on your watch list.
Zorko had his lowest so far this year but there were only 5 players in this game over 100 so nothing to be concerned about. His efficiency was what caused the low score at 60%.
Zorko was the best for the Lions with his 30 disposals and 11 marks. The ball was in his area with the Swans pressing and he is still someone we could pivot to after his bye.
Zorko continues to defy his age with a huge game to be the best for the Lions. We saw no reason that he won't be a great selection again this season.

injury_suspension_status_text: ACL. Out for season.

notes.note: Cerra's second game was better than the first with 7 tackles included but he isn't doing enough to make us consider him.
8 kicks and 17 handballs for Cripps as he led the game with 15 contested possessions. His first under 100 in the last three but he was not far away as he continues to post a great run of scores.

Cripps went head to head with Harley Reid and had a big game with 31 disposals and a goal. He had the most contested possessions in the game with 16. He is in a solid run of form of late and a good pick up.
Cripps racked up 31 touches and led the game with 16 contested possessions. The skipper has been over 110 in 5 of his last 6 now.
This was Crippa's first under 100 in the last five games as he was tagged by Setterfield. His score wasn't great for three quarters but a 41 point last really boosted him.
Cripps stood up and kicked the winning goal as he had 30 disposals and led the game with 8 clearances. His fourth over 110 in a row.
Cripps starred with 29 disposals and 2 goals whilst leading the game in contested possessions and clearances. Back to back 100+ for the first time this year.
This was Cripps best score this season but it was also just his third over 100. Of his 32 disposals only 9 were kicks. He did have team high 9 clearances and 18 contested possessions.
Cripps continues with his higher handball to kick ratio. 7 kicks to 18 handballs. Second lowest score of the season for him despite his 5 clearances which was an equal team high.
Cripps spent some time on the bench at a crucial point but his game was solid with 29 disposals and 9 tackles. But 4 free kicks against hurt his score. His value is dropping so you can wait on him.
Cripps was in his handball heavy game again with 2/3rds of his disposals being b hand. He was under pressure with 15 contested possessions and an efficiency of just 57%.

Parish did have 17 disposals but there were 6 clangers which didn't help and he finished with his second below 40 in a row.
Parish did have 15 touches but a 53% efficiency and 2 free kicks given away and 6 clangers meant he had his worst score of the season. Not what we wanted.
Parish came back into the side this week with 25 disposals. This was below his average and if you held then he is one you should be looking to upgrade.
Parish posted his equal lowest score of the season with this being the third 67 for him. Hopefully this is not a regression back to these scores regularly.

Parish was everywhere in the middle ending with 9 clearances and 16 contested possessions to go with 41 disposals and 7 marks. If not for 5 free kicks given away this score could have been even higher!
Parish was the top scoring Bomber with his 25 disposals at 84% resulting in his third 100+ score for the season.
Parish returned this week with 23 touches and a goal. He hit his BE but with some 100+ scores dropping out of his score cycle he is now over 100 for a BE so you should look at trading.
Parish was rested this week.
This was his lowest in the last four games with 15 of his 23 disposals being handballs. Hopefully this score isn't a sign of things to come.
Again Parish has delivered after he was traded out a couple of weeks ago by a lot of teams. 30 disposals 11 clearances and 15 contested possessions shows why many started with him.
Parish was hotly traded out this week and of course that led to a huge score and his best of the season from 34 disposals. Certainly not time to bring him in though.
Parish got to his BE but only just with 19 disposals. He can be traded whenever you are able as this looks to be his ceiling.
Back to back scores in the mid 60s for Parish. We expected more from him and with a new BE of 71 we may need to consider getting out this week.

Parish didn't have a big outing but did get his hands on the footy with 24 disposals it was just that only 66% were effective. The Bombers mids were under immense pressure but this is likely to be the case every week.
Parish returned with a bang in the first term but did slow down from there. He finished well with 21 disposals. In 46% of sides don't rush to move him on.
Roberts had his first under 100 since round 1 in the wet conditions. He had 30 disposals which is down on what he has been doing but still good. Nothing to be concerned about.
Ridley suffered a calf issue in the third and looks set for another stint on the sidelines.
Ridley is going to miss up to 5 weeks with a calf injury.
Roberts was back and he had the second best score for the Bombers with his 23 disposals. A good return and result for those that held.
Roberts suffered a dislocated shoulder and left the game in the second term. This will be yet another forced trade for many coaches as he looks like missing significant time.
The key to Roberts first score over 100 in the last four games was the efficiency with his 22 disposals going at 86%.
Roberts had the tag from Murdock this week as we thought may happen. He finished with 31 disposals with 10 being from kick ins. He did give away 4 free kicks which hurt him.

Roberts was quiet in the first term but did find the footy after that. His role was moved around a bit with the injuries the Dons had early in the game. He missed his BE but he will be a fine hold still.

Huge night for Archie with 42 disposals and 11 marks to top score in the game. This was his best of the season and he has shown how good he is in that half back role. He is one you can consider for a VC or C.
Roberts kept his streak alive but only just. 27 disposals at 77% as he was only one of just three Bombers to reach 100 in the heavy loss.

Roberts was fantastic yet again with his 42 disposals and 9 marks. He is a must have in defence. His price is rising sharply so time to get him or you will have to wait for one poor score to bring it down.
Roberts continues to deliver and he is fast becoming too expensive for us to bring in if we don't have him. 24 kicks 9 handballs and 7 marks. He is looking like a top 6 defender.
Roberts has been on fire of late after that poor first round. But the last two have been 130+. Will be a popular selection while the Bombers are playing this style of game.
We didn't see this one coming! Huge from Roberts with 29 kicks 8 handballs and 12 marks for his third over 100 in a row which has seen his BE land at 50.
This is another great outing from Roberts with his second 100+ score in a row. This is more what we expected when many people were picking him at the start of the season.

This is the sort of game we expected from Roberts when we picked him for round 1. 26 disposals and 11 contested possessions. His BE of 106 means he isn't going to make us some big cash. So we need big scores to keep him.

Roberts was popular across the preseason and ended in 9% of teams. He didn't reach the level that we were hoping from his 20 disposals at 65%. We have another week before his price changes so you can wait for one more.
Roberts has been a preseason hype player and one that you may want to look into for your starting squad.
Best in the last three for Robey from his 18 disposals and goal. This is about the most we should expect from him each week and anything beyond that is a bonus.
This was Robey's lowest since round 7 and he missed his BE with just 3 kicks and 6 handballs. This is a concern as his BE has jumped to 102 so you will want to trade.
Robey beat his BE and had 15 disposals. He did give away 3 frees which hurt. He has that 92 in his cycle for another week so his BE remains low at 49 but he needs another big score to keep it there.
This was one better than his season high from a couple of weeks back as he racked up 19 disposals and 9 clearances. This score means that he will keep his low BE for a couple more weeks.

Robey was a very popular trade in this week with his recent form and low BE. This was his third in the 60s in the last four and as a result his BE remains low at 13. He is just a bit too expensive now to be downgraded to.
Robey had a great game with 2 goals the result of his 22 disposals. His last three have been his best scores this year so his BE remains negative.
Robey has had two in the 60s in a row now and his BE is now down at -11 meaning he could be a handy downgrade despite having already risen in value.
Robey was quiet with his 9 disposals and his scoring isn't looking like he will make us much money.
This was Robey's second game and he has a 28 and now a 50. His BE of 22 isn't screaming pick me and there are better options for us.
Sharp left the game in the third with what looked to be a bad shoulder injury. Watch the injury reports to see how long he is out for.
Sharp had his best score of the season so far with his 19 disposals at 84%. This dropped his BE to 2 so if you think he will hold his spot then you could get him in.
Sharp was a late out as many expected with injury.
Sharp left the game in the third quarter with an ankle injury and his score ensures that he won't be the money maker we had hoped. Trade before he plays again.

First gamer Sharp got to his score with the assistance of 2 goals. The pleasing part was the 4 tackles but there were only 6 possessions. We need him to keep kicking goals but he could be a short burn for us.
Tsatas continued his good run of scoring with a 22 possession game. If he keeps scoring like this he will be one to possibly hold through his bye as good bench cover.
Another great score from Tsatas as he continues to show that he is a talent and a good SuperCoach scorer. 25 disposals and he led the Bombers in clearances with 7.
Tsatas came back into the side after missing 4 games. He showed that he should have been in before now with his 26 disposals including 9 contested possessions.
Tsatas had a great game in the VFL and must be considered for this week's game by Essendon.
Elijah didn't deliver what those that brought him in this week were hoping for but with his BE he is certainly still of value to your side. He still had 18 disposals so he should be ok.
This is two solid scores now for Tsatas and a BE of -49. He will be amongst the most traded in.
Bolton was electric in the third term with 40 of his points coming then. He had 23 disposals and a couple of goals.
Just the one goal for Bolton but because he used the footy well at 95% for his 20 disposals saw him stay up in a decent scoring position.
Bolton had the second most CBAs for the game for the Dockers as he had 26 disposals but didn't hit the scoreboard. He can be up and down so just be careful selecting him.
18 touches for Bolton at 72%. This is now three under 90 in the last four for him.
Bolton didn't hit the scoreboard but didn't need to with 27 disposals and 7 marks in the big win.
Bolton didn't get in on the goal scoring and registered 21 disposals and whilst it was his best in the last three it wasn't up where we would have hoped in a Docker win.

Just one goal for Bolton (which was outstanding) to go with 25 disposals at 60%. He hasn't been able to consistently deliver 90+ scores this season with this his lowest in the last five and second in the 70s in a row.
Bolton did kick 2 goals but the conditions didn't help him as it was a scrappy game at times and not free flowing as he likes it. A good result given his 54% efficiency.

Bolton was quiet for three quarters with less than 20 points in each term but like the Dockers he came to life in the last quarter with 47 points. After two big scores this wasn't a bad one but it is a concern that he needed a big quarter to get him there.
Bolton has again had back to back scores over 130 with his 30 disposals. Whilst he has four over 130 he also has three under 70 and that is what we get from him. Feast or Famine.
Bolton can be feast or famine. He has been under 70 in his previous two but this week put up 33 disposals 8 tackles and a couple of goals as he matched his season high.
Bolton backed up his good score with his 33 disposals and interestingly this didn't include any goals. He had 71% CBAs for the second week in a row.
This was the best we have seen from Bolton as a Docker for a while. Just 2 goals but 32 disposals and an equal game high 9 clearances.

Brayshaw had the Jordon tag for much of the game before he was released late but he managed to be the top scorer for the Dockers with his 25 disposals. We aren't used to seeing him get the tag. Hopefully this doesn't become a trend
Brayshaw couldn't keep that hot run of 100+ going but he still was good with his 22 disposals and 8 tackles.
Andy Brayshaw was the star for the Dockers as he took 9 marks and had 29 disposals which resulted in his best score of the year and fourth 110+ in a row.
Great game for Brayshaw as this is three in a row over 100 as he is really hitting some great form. 35 disposals and 7 tackles as he was great through the middle for the Dockers.
Brayshaw was one of the best for the game with his 30 disposals and 9 clearances being the best for the game. Back to back in the 120s is a good sign whilst Serong is out.

Brayshaw continues his run of scores in the 90s with a 25 disposals performance. He did have the equal most clearances for the Dockers with 7. He isn't hitting those ceiling scores often enough for us.
This is now back to back in the 90s for Brayshaw he has been good of late and is on the edge of being one we may want. 26 disposals at 88% in the wet is a good result.
24 disposals for Brayshaw with 18 of them being effective. He also attended the most Centre Ball Ups than any other Docker. His Scoring is just too inconsistent for us.
Brayshaw still hasn't been able to string two 100+ games in a row. 22 disposals and 8 tackles for him.
10 tackles for Brayshaw for his best in the last three games. He was the main man out of the middle with Serong being tagged.
Brayshaw copped an early cork and it did affect his score with him ending on just 65. His scoring isn't at the level that we would like so he isn't one you want to bring in at the moment.

Brayshaw had a quiet game in the wet with no marks but 9 tackles and 19 disposals. The wet conditions affected his efficiency which was just 47%. He wasn't on our radar but this will see him off it for a bit longer.
This is two in the 120s for Brayshaw in his four games. We would just like to see some consistency for him to be a solid selection.
Brayshaw is still going to lose value so if he is one you are looking at just hold off still. He is also not scoring consistently high enough for us to be at the top of the shopping list.
Much better for Brayshaw with 39 disposals this week and a goal. It would be prudent to see another good score from him before bringing him in.
Brayshaw had an afternoon to forget with 4 free kicks against and just 14 touches. You can still wait a week before you have to trade him to ensure he doesn't lose money.
Clark slotted a goal to go with his 23 disposals as this makes it three over 90 in a row now which is positive for owners.
Clark dropped back below 100 making this three in the last four now. 23 disposals at 87% for him this week.
This was just his second over 100 in the last 9 weeks. He did have 24 disposals as the Dockers dominated this game. He may be a risk to trade into until we see this more regularly.
This was the lowest we have seen from Clark since round 4 as he had 17 disposals and 5 marks. There was a very even spread of points across the Dockers.
The ball wasn't in Clark's area too often leading to him dropping back below 100 this week.
24 touches for Clark for his first over 100 in the last 6 games. A solid outing as the Dockers controlled that part of the ground.

It's been 5 scores under 100 now for Clark in a row since that huge score in round 6. He put up 18 disposals at 88%  in what was a fairly even scoring game from Fremantle. Don't jump off but we may look to upgrade across the byes.
Clark had his best score in the last four weeks  from his 22 disposals.
Clark has now had three in a row under 90 which came from 19 disposals. His value is dropping as is his average.
After his great run his last two haven't been fantastic for Clark owners. But 3 free kicks against did hurt his score. Not time to move him but he is a watch.
Clark's run of great scoring has been interrupted by this week's 25 disposal 6 mark game. He seems to have a quieter score every few weeks recently but he should be ok to hold.
Clark top scored for the game by a big margin. Despite two poor scores he has had a good season other than that. He is still looking a good option.
Clark seems to have returned to the high possession game we have seen and apart from the previous week's poor one he has been scoring well. His price is dropping so keep an eye on him.
Clark has now put together two great games in a row and is looking to be back to the scoring we saw a couple of seasons ago. 27 disposals at 81% for him this week in the wet.
Jackson had just 3 kicks with 14 handballs. But he also had game highs in contested possessions with 14 and equal high clearances with 7. A tough match up and this was a good performance.
2 goals from 12 disposals for Jackson with his 31 hit outs. Not a huge score from him but still solid for owners. Darcy didn't have a big score so there is a chance that experiment may end.
Jackson was again outstanding with his two goals and 4 clearances. He is still a great option for your sides as his game is a very SuperCoach friendly one.

The complete all round game from Jackson. He finished with 28 disposals and had 9 tackles as he led the game in contested possessions with 15 and added a game high 6 clearances.  He is one that many other coaches will be looking at.
Jackson was back to his best after a quieter week. He dominated the ruck and amassed 19 clearances and kicked 3 goals.
Jackson battled against Draper and posted his second under 100 in the last three weeks. Just the 15 disposals for him.
Jackson had a tougher night than normal against Marshall and De Koning and after a quiet first term he did come good with 18 contested possessions and 7 clearances to go with 22 disposals.
Jackson was very quiet in the first half with just 16 points at the half but a 35 point third term helped us. The conditions weren't kind to him so don't worry about this one.

Jackson was outstanding and had his third 140+ score in a row now as he lit up the last 5 mins of the game to get the Dockers over the line. He had 49 points in the last term and if you can get him in he is a VC and C option each week.

Jackson is the one player we must have this season. This is back to back 140+ scores and his third of that mark this season. He had 18 disposals but he dominated the hit outs with 36 and had 12 contested possessions.
Jackson is having a season out of the box with another best on ground performance with 31 hitouts 2 goals and 22 disposals. He is one that you must consider.
Jackson had his way with the inexperienced Eagles rucks. His last three have now been either 125 or 126. He is a great option. Whilst Darcy is out of the side he is playing that scoring friendly role
Jackson had to play in ruck for most of the game after Darcy left the game early. He is having a stellar season so far and will be the number 1 ruck with Darcy out this week.

Jackson top scored for the Dockers and nearly made his high BE. He was great in the ruck and often took the ball and cleared it having 14 contested possessions and 7 clearances. One you have to consider.
Jackson kept his 100+ streak going. Certainly has been a great selection for our sides and he is one that we should be looking at getting and particularly if he gets DPP.
Jackson spent time as a midfielder as well as a ruck again this week as he continues to post some big scores. He could be the answer as one of your two rucks this season.

Jackson was someone that floated in and out of a lot of R2 positions during preseason and those that stuck with him were rewarded. Big game with 18 contested possession and 10 clearances to lead the game in both categories.

injury_suspension_status_text: Finger. Expected to be available for round 22.

notes.note: Reid took a bit to get going but he fired up before getting the tag from Jordon in the last term and was held to just 10 points in that quarter. He did have 28 disposals at 85%.
Reid has been on a good run of scoring recently and shows no sign of slowing down. 19 disposals for him with his 8 contested possessions.
Reid continues to show he is a great option in your forward line with his 28 disposals this week.
Reid is putting together a fantastic second season with his 27 disposals this week and he was one of just three Dockers over 100 this week. His first back to back weeks over 100 this year.
Reid has now had two over 120 in the last three but that other score was a concern. He looked good with his 23 disposals yielding 2 goals.
A very quiet second term from Reid as he finished with 21 disposals. This was his lowest score since round 3.

30 disposals and 9 contested possessions for Reid as he was one of the ones that got the Dockers up and running in the last quarter. This was just his second score over 100 for the season and he equal top scored in this game.
A late goal for Reid went with his 30 disposals but the efficiency was down in the wet at 63%.

1.2 for Reid from his 20 disposals. He was one of the catalysts in that last term that helped get the win for the Dockers. His scoring is hanging around the 70s and 80s which makes him almost a keeper.
Reid's scoring has plateaued lately with a couple of scores in the70s in a row. If you got him for cash generation he has topped out at the moment and with Young back he has less CBAs.
Reid hasn't had the big scores this season but he is still scoring well however this was his lowest in the last four games.
Reid had his second best score of the season so far from his 26 disposals. He remains a good forward option.
Reid is showing his value to this Docker side with 22 disposals in the wet. Just the efficiency hurt him in this game like most players in the game.
Reid is an impressive young player and had 26 disposals and 5 tackles. He is one you can consider but he will be a must have in years to come.
Reid was quiet this week and really dropped down from his first two scores. He saw plenty of the footy with 23 touches but his usage included 8 clangers.
Reid was the third best scorer for the Dockers as he was talked about a lot this year. He had 41% CBAs and looks to have a great role.
Ryan was the best scorer in the game with 10 marks in the wet to go with 23 kicks and a couple of handballs. By far his best this season so don't jump on yet until we see another good score.
28 touches for Serong and back to back 100+ for him. The issue is that in his previous two games were both under 90.
Best from Serong for the last three games with his 31 disposals and 14 contested possessions. If not for the low efficiency of 54% he would have put up a big score.
Serong did have 20 disposals but it was Brayshaw that had the big role this week. His price has dropped and is likely to drop further with a new BE of 132.
Serong returned this week and did have his minutes managed playing just 66% time on ground but he still had 22 disposals.
Serong was one of the four Dockers over 100 thanks to his 24 disposals as he led the game in contested possessions with 15 and led the Dockers in clearances with 6.
28 touches for Serong with his first score over 100 since round 4. He had the most clearances for the Dockers. Hopefully this is a sign of things to come.
This is now four games in a row under 100 for Serong and this is a concern because three of them have been under 90 and this was his lowest for the season.
Serong was being tagged by Lord and while he still had 22 disposals he went at just 50% due to the pressure of that tag. This was his third sub 100 score in a row.
24 touches for Serong and he had the most clearances in the game at 6. Whilst it is two under 100 in a row it wasn't by much.
Spent the second half running with Daicos and managed 24 disposals but his efficiency was just 62% in the wet. His second lowest this year. The conditions didn't suit so don't panic on him.
Serong did as he pleased with his 32 disposals with 8 tackles. He is pushing to be a part of your best 8 midfield in your Supercoach team.
Big last term for Serong where he really boosted his scoring with a couple of goals and 32 disposals to go with 6 tackles.
Serong copped the tag from Tholstrup this week after last week's big game. Just the 16 disposals which let Brayshaw off the chain. This could be a common factor during the season.
Serong top scored in the game thanks to 13 contested possessions and 30 disposals. He wasn't consistent throughout the game but he got the job done for the Dockers.

injury_suspension_status_text: Quad. Expected to be available for round 22.

notes.note: Treacy kicked 4.4 as along with other Dockers he was off line early. This was his first over 100 since round 12.
Treacy was wayward early but did end with 2.2 and he had just the 8 kicks and the 1 handball which is down from what we have seen from him lately.
Treacy started strong and finished with 3 goals from 7 marks and 16 disposals. He is on a fantastic run of scoring.

Treacy was the star for the Dockers and has now got 4 over 100 in a row and this was his fifth over 120 this season. He is not highly owned so could be a very handy unique for you. 11 marks 2 goals and 19 disposals this week.
Treacy was huge for the Dockers. 4 goals from his 12 marks and 16 disposals. This is now two big scores in a row for him. Keep a watching brief on him.
Voss slotted 4 goals from 20 touches and 10 marks as he has put up three good scores now in the last four weeks.

injury_suspension_status_text: Calf. Subject to fitness test.
Groin. Subject to fitness test.

notes.note: Young can't get a run at it with a groin injury for him this week as he left the game with just 10 disposals. He looks to be a trade unfortunately.
Young had just 69% time on ground and we saw his lowest score of the season with 13 disposals.
Young still played limited time with 67% and he left the ground with a knock to the shin in the third term but he did return and finish out the game with 15 disposals.
Young was back this week and had a good hit out from just 66% time on ground. 23 disposals and a couple of goals in the dominant Docker win.
Young did some great work in the last quarter but did have just the 15 disposals. He still hasn't gone under 80 but there is just the one over 100. Hopefully he keeps building.
3 goals for Young and 20 disposals with 7 tackles. His best so far and he had 51% CBAs. But just beware as we won�t be surprised if he does get some rests to ensure he doesn't reinjure himself.

Young has now put a couple of games in a row together now. He ahs had now three games in the 80s this season. He could take a while to get back to his best after his injuries so don't expect huge scores just yet.
Young's return was a solid one with 23 disposals. He isn't a must get this week even though his price will move next week. He also played just 66% time on ground.
Young was a question mark all week as to whether he would play but he did and scored well enough for us. Getting through the game was the key for us.
Noah saw enough of the footy with 25 touches but just 56% efficiency for him is what really held his score down.
Anderson did have 20 touches and a goal but this was easily his lowest for 8 weeks as it was also his first under 100 in that period.
Anderson had 33 disposals and had 8 marks. He continues to be a great option for the midfield since his early season operation.
Anderson was massive with 43 disposals and 6 marks showing that he was a great pick after that surgery. He has only been under 125 once in the last 6 games.
Anderson relished the fact that Mullin went to Petracca instead f him and had a big first half being on 81 at the half. He racked up 11 tackles to go with his 29 disposals.
Anderson was one of just three Suns to reach triple figures. 25 disposals and a team high 12 contested possessions for him. He is one that will be targeted off his bye.
Anderson racked up 23 kicks and 8 handballs to go with a goal. This made it three in a row over 100 for him for the first time this season.
Anderson was one of the best for the Suns with 11 contested disposals and 8 clearances. From his 33 touches. This is what we had hoped for when we brought him in.
Anderson was huge with 31 disposals at 80% and 10 marks in the slippery Darwin conditions. This was his first over 100 since round 1.
27 touches for Noah with just 5 contested possessions. His scoring isn't going consistently over 100 which means he is a liability for your midfield.
Anderson with his 31 disposals posted his best in a few weeks. Unfortunately he isn't delivering those big scores we hoped for.
Anderson missed this week following appendix surgery. Wait for team sheets to see if he will be back.
Anderson had the Jordon tag for the first half and parts of the third term. He has had his appendix out this week so will miss at least this week and possibly another.
Lowest of the season for Anderson and second under 100 in a row. It wasn't a great day for him with his 22 disposals coming at 72%.
21 disposals for Anderson and just missing the 100. If we have no Petracca when they return from bye he will shoulder the bulk of the load in that midfield but he will also get extra attention.
Anderson took full advantage of the match up against the Eagles. He managed 34 disposals and a goal. He is going to be another great selection this year.
Anderson looked very good and could be a good pick for you. He kicked 1.4 so his score could have been so much more.

injury_suspension_status_text: Foot. Subject to fitness test.
Ankle. Subject to fitness test.
Shoulder. Expected recovery time is to be confirmed.

Knee. Out for season.

notes.note: Not a great night for Humphrey with just the 9 disposals and he gave away 3 free kicks.
Humphrey spent more time up forward with Petracca in the midfield and as a result he kicked 4 goals. This won't happen every week so just temper any expectations.
Lombard had his best score since round 10 with 21 disposals and a goal this week. He has been doing enough to hold him. He is an F6 at best but hopefully he is your bench cover.
Lombard had his lowest since round 6. He is a F6 at the best for your side and if you can loop him that would be the best option for your side.
Lombard hasn't dipped below 60 since the bye and this makes him a great bench cover as we see the season through as we run out of trades.

Lombard keeps hanging around in a lot of teams and his 2 goals really helped that sore this week as he  rose in value again. He is possibly one that is scoring well enough to be retained as your bench cover or loop option up forward.
Lombard posted his best score in the last three games and continued his rise in value. Whilst he may rise more he is one you should be looking to upgrade when you can.

Lombard has been a good scorer of late and is providing some value through the byes. If you still hold him he is going to raise in value a bit more but if you have a good upgrade that uses him then do it.
Lombard was back to his regular scoring level with 12 disposals. His BE remains low at 26 so should make some more cash but if you wanted to move him you can.
Lombard had one of his better games and highest score for the year by more than 20 points. 18 disposals and a goal. This saw his BE drop to 17 so you can hold.
Lombard had his second over 50 in a row and made his BE comfortably. His new one of 23 is a good sign for owners and we can keep him til the byes.

Lombard had one of his best games of the season and comfortably got his BE. This has bought him some more time in our sides with a new BE of 20. He won't score like this every week but the BE means we can hold.
Lombard got his BE with a 13 disposal game. But his new BE of 32 means he is on the cusp of needing to be traded.
Lombard has now had three solid games in a row. He won't post huge scores but this seems to be about his range. Probably one more week for him before he starts to lose cash with the BE of 25
Lombard managed 12 disposals and it wasn't his worst game as he did beat his BE. But a new one of 3 means you can hold him a little longer. But plan your escape route.
Lombard had 18 disposals but 14 were by hand with this being his best in the last three. A BE of 26 means we can hold for at least one more week.
11 disposals and 3 free kicks against saw a very low score from Lombard. With his new BE at 13 and the bye this week you could be forgiven for trading as the role wasn't great.
Lombard had a very slow start to the game but did get going but his score was impacted by a couple of goals from his 11 disposals. Not the score we hoped for but he was good for his value.
Lombard has been a popular selection and a couple of goals contributed to his score. He passed the eye test as he certainly looked at home. Pick with confidence.
Lots of handballs for Touk with 15 to go with his 9 kicks. This is now two under 80 in a row for him and four under 90 in the last five.
Miller seemed to get a lot of the footy but 18 of his 25 disposals were by hand which meant his score wasn't as high as many thought it may have been.
We didn't know what role Touk would have with the midfield big 3 all playing but he found a way to score and attended just 25% CBAs. Which was the 7th in line for the Suns.
Touk racked up 31 disposals to be one of 7 Suns to hit 100 this week. First back to back over that mark for him since rounds 1 and 2.
Miller racked up 26 disposals as he also picked up some of the disposals that were left on the table by Anderson.
We expected Touk to get the uptick with Petracca out of the side but he was the one that copped the Tholstrup tag but still managed 21 disposals.
With Petracca missing at least 4 weeks we could see Touk get an uptick in possessions and points.
Murray's second game was a fruitful one with 19 disposals. The problem is his price as a downgrade isn't ideal with there being better options at $99k.
18 disposals for Noble in a quieter game from him. His last four games have been very inconsistent in terms of scoring for him.
Noble was much better this week after two quieter games. 13 marks and 33 disposals at 84%. It was a big third quarter that really helped his score.
